title: Just arrived in ICU on the ED ventilator settings
summary: A 61-year-old with severe pneumonia and bilateral infiltrates has been intubated in the ED and arrives hypoxaemic on 650 mL tidal volumes.

evidence.claim: Tidal volume 6 mL/kg predicted body weight with plateau pressure 30 cmH2O or less reduced mortality compared with 12 mL/kg
evidence.source: ARDS Network. Ventilation with lower tidal volumes as compared with traditional tidal volumes for acute lung injury and ARDS. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1301-8

evidence.claim: Driving pressure (plateau minus PEEP) was the ventilation variable most strongly associated with survival; risk rose above about 15 cmH2O
evidence.source: Amato MBP, et al. Driving pressure and survival in the acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med 2015;372:747-55

evidence.claim: Early prolonged prone positioning (16 h or more a day) reduced mortality in ARDS with PaO2/FiO2 below 150 on FiO2 0.6 or more and PEEP 5 or more
evidence.source: Guérin C, et al. Prone positioning in severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSEVA). N Engl J Med 2013;368:2159-68

evidence.claim: Recommendations for low tidal volume, plateau pressure limits and prone positioning in moderate to severe ARDS
evidence.source: Grasselli G, et al. ESICM guidelines on acute respiratory distress syndrome: definition, phenotyping and respiratory support strategies. Intensive Care Med 2023;49:727-59

evidence.claim: ATS guideline: low tidal volume and plateau pressure limits, prone positioning for severe ARDS, higher PEEP without lung recruitment manoeuvres for moderate to severe ARDS
evidence.source: Qadir N, et al. An update on management of adult patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome: an official ATS clinical practice guideline. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2024;209:24-36

evidence.claim: Severity bands by PaO2/FiO2 on PEEP 5 or more: mild 200-300, moderate 100-200, severe 100 or less
evidence.source: ARDS Definition Task Force. Acute respiratory distress syndrome: the Berlin definition. JAMA 2012;307:2526-33

patient.presentingStory: Intubated in the ED 30 minutes ago for worsening hypoxaemia with pneumonia. Rocuronium was given for intubation and he is sedated on propofol and fentanyl. The ED set the ventilator to 650 mL. He has just been transferred onto your ICU ventilator with the same settings.
patient.history: Hypertension, obesity, otherwise well. Five days of cough and fever. Chest X-ray in ED showed bilateral infiltrates. Echo in ED: good LV function. Height 170 cm, weight 98 kg. Full escalation.

orderEffects.note: Prone positioning improves V/Q matching; modelled as a gradual fall in shunt

actions.text: He's prone. Lines, tube and pressure areas checked.
What's his predicted body weight, and what plateau and driving pressure is he on now?

findings.examine: Sedated and paralysed, synchronous with the ventilator. Equal air entry, coarse crackles bilaterally. Tube at 23 cm at the lips. Warm peripheries, capillary refill 3 s. No wheeze.
findings.cxr: Endotracheal tube 4 cm above the carina. Bilateral patchy airspace opacities, worse on the right. No pneumothorax. Central line tip in the SVC.

then.detail: SpO2 stayed above 95% on an FiO2 over 0.5 for 30 minutes. The ARDSNet target is 88 to 95%: wean the oxygen.
Proned before tidal volume was reduced. Set lung-protective ventilation first, then reassess oxygenation.
Plateau pressure above 30 cmH2O for 30+ minutes in ARDS.
Tidal volume above 8 mL/kg predicted body weight for 30+ minutes. Tidal volume is set by predicted (height-based) weight, not actual weight.

then.text: He has been on these settings for 20 minutes. Reassess him. What is your next step?
Sats have been in the 70s for a quarter of an hour and his heart rate keeps climbing.
He's still desaturated. What is your plan for his oxygenation?

then.reason: Severe hypoxaemia persisted for 30 minutes without correction.
Stable on lung-protective ventilation with acceptable oxygenation and pH.

then.text: Doctor, his colour is worse and he looks very unwell. Can you come and look?
He looks a bit pinker and the ventilator seems to be struggling less. I'll keep watching him.
He's much the same as when he came to us. I'll keep watching him.

predictionPoints.question: Before touching the ventilator: what is his predicted body weight? (male, 170 cm)
predictionPoints.explanation: PBW (male) = 50 + 0.91 × (height in cm − 152.4) = 50 + 0.91 × 17.6 ≈ 66 kg. So 6 mL/kg is about 400 mL and 8 mL/kg about 530 mL. The 650 mL he arrived on is about 9.8 mL/kg PBW, even though it is only 6.6 mL/kg of his actual weight.

predictionPoints.question: You have just changed the ventilator. Once things settle, which way will each of these go?
predictionPoints.explanation: Plateau pressure = PEEP + VT/compliance. Lowering VT lowers it. In a recruitable lung, raising PEEP recruits collapsed alveoli, increasing compliance and lowering driving pressure, but excessive PEEP can cause overdistension. A lower VT cuts alveolar ventilation unless the rate rises enough, so PaCO2 tends to rise. More PEEP usually improves oxygenation in recruitable lung. The engine marks this against what actually happened with your settings.

predictionPoints.question: Twenty minutes on protective settings. What is the next step for his oxygenation?
options: Prone positioning for 16 hours or more a day
predictionPoints.answerKey: Prone positioning for 16 hours or more a day
predictionPoints.explanation: PROSEVA showed lower mortality with early prolonged proning when P/F was below 150. Inhaled nitric oxide improves oxygenation without a survival benefit, and high-frequency oscillation (OSCILLATE) and staircase recruitment manoeuvres (ART) were associated with harm.

rubric.description: Weaned FiO2 once SpO2 was above 95%
Reduced tidal volume to 8 mL/kg PBW or less within 30 minutes (target about 6)
Kept plateau pressure at 30 cmH2O or less (no prolonged breach)
Kept driving pressure at 15 cmH2O or less, or tidal volume at 6.5 mL/kg PBW or less
Raised PEEP to 10 cmH2O or more within the first hour while keeping driving pressure at 15 cmH2O or less
Checked a blood gas after changing settings (2 or more within 90 minutes)
pH 7.20 or higher at the end, with rate rather than tidal volume used to clear CO2
Proned for P/F below 150 despite protective settings

keyPoints: Set tidal volume by predicted body weight (height and sex), not actual weight. He is 66 kg PBW: 6 mL/kg is about 400 mL.

Check plateau pressure with an inspiratory hold and keep it at 30 cmH2O or less. Lower driving pressure (plateau minus PEEP) is associated with lower mortality in ARDS (Amato, NEJM 2015); many units aim for 15 cmH2O or less.
Raise the rate to offset the lower tidal volume. Some hypercapnia is acceptable (permissive hypercapnia), usually keeping pH at 7.20 or above.
Use PEEP for oxygenation in recruitable lung. At a fixed tidal volume, every cmH2O of PEEP adds to plateau pressure.
If P/F stays below 150 despite optimised settings, prone early for 16 hours or more a day (PROSEVA).
In recruitable ARDS, titrating PEEP balances alveolar recruitment (improving compliance and lowering driving pressure) against overdistension at high volumes (raising driving pressure).
Prone positioning is for a P/F ratio below 150 on protective settings, in sessions of about 16 hours (PROSEVA).
